request.question: Which cost elements ran over budget last quarter?

answer:
Last quarter (Q1 FY2027, Jul–Sep 2026) saw **three cost elements over budget**: Diesel (+USD 400k, +2.4%), Tyres (+USD 456k, +13.8%), and an unbudgeted Maintenance Order spend of USD 4.3M.

| Cost Element | Budget (USD) | Actual (USD) | Variance (USD) | Variance (%) | Provenance |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Diesel** | 16,857,425 | 17,257,904 | +400,480 | +2.4% | SAP_STANDIN |
| **Tyres** | 3,312,000 | 3,767,552 | +455,552 | +13.8% | SAP_STANDIN |
| **Maintenance Order** | 0 | 4,308,634 | +4,308,634 | n/a | SAP_STANDIN |

The Tyres overrun of 13.8% and the unbudgeted maintenance spike warrant immediate investigation—potential causes include unplanned equipment failures, supplier price changes, or accelerated wear. Conversely, Explosives (−5.1%), Fleet Maintenance (−2.3%), Rail (−5.5%), Port (−5.5%), Processing (−4.8%), and Power (−3.6%) all came in under budget.

**Next step:** Drill into the Maintenance Order postings and tyre invoices to isolate root causes (e.g., specific asset failures, cycle-time impacts) and assess whether the variance signals a structural cost-per-tonne risk for Q2 FY2027.

---

**Sources** *(simulated data for a fictional operator)*  
**SAP_STANDIN:** Budget and cost postings for Q1 FY2027 cost elements—CONTRACTORS, DIESEL, EXPLOSIVES, FLEET_MAINTENANCE, LABOUR, MAINTENANCE_ORDER, PORT, POWER, PROCESSING, RAIL, SITE_G_AND_A, TYRES.
